milestone.title: mp init AGENTS.md gaps — stale templates, missing cross-links, and unresolvable doc refs in consumer projects

intent.outcome: mp init produces correct, self-contained agent instructions that an agent can follow without missing doc references or stale paths, regardless of whether the project already has a root AGENTS.md.

problem.description: On consumer projects that adopt master-plan, the agent-instruction surface shipped by `mp init` is broken in four ways. (1) ROOT-AGENTS-SNIPPET.md uses project-relative `docs/...` references that don't resolve against the actual installed toolkit (~/.agents/master-plan/), so agents in consumer projects follow stale paths. (2) AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md does the same with `../docs/...` references — the project doesn't have a docs/ tree with mp content. (3) `mp init` silently skips when a root AGENTS.md already exists, so the user thinks init worked but the agent is missing critical instructions (or has stale ones). (4) There's no refresh path — once init has run, picking up template fixes requires manual surgery. The net effect: agents in consumer projects follow stale or unresolvable doc paths, leading to confused behavior or silent failures when they try to look up mp commands.

in_scope: Fix ROOT-AGENTS-SNIPPET.md doc references to match the installed toolkit layout
Decide what docs AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md should reference (toolkit-absolute paths vs project-relative) and fix them
Make mp init handle existing root AGENTS.md: warn, offer --force / --merge, or append the snippet
Add mp init --refresh to re-write master-plan/AGENTS.md from the current binary's template (or add a doctor check)
out_of_scope: Restructuring the installed toolkit docs tree (that's a separate documentation project)
Auto-updating root AGENTS.md on every mp command (too invasive)

design_decisions.choice: Use toolkit-absolute paths (~/.agents/master-plan/docs/...) in templates, not project-relative ../docs/...
design_decisions.rationale: The installed toolkit is the canonical location for mp docs. Consumer projects don't have a docs/ directory with mp content. Toolkit-absolute paths survive regardless of where the project is checked out.

design_decisions.choice: Warn + print the snippet to stdout with instructions, offer --force flag to overwrite
design_decisions.rationale: Silently skipping is the worst behavior — the user thinks init worked but the agent is missing critical instructions. Overwriting without asking is destructive. Printing the snippet lets the user manually merge.

open_questions.question: Should we also vendor a minimal subset of toolkit docs into the project's master-plan/ so that doc references work even offline? Or rely entirely on the toolkit installation path?
open_questions.answer: Rely on toolkit-absolute paths (~/.agents/master-plan/docs/...) per the in-scope design decision. Vendoring a minimal subset into the project would duplicate content, drift from the canonical docs, and break the consumer-surface hygiene rule (templates/skills/** and templates/AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md must be self-contained without internal provenance). Trade-off accepted: offline use cases would need a separate mechanism — out of scope for M194; if needed, file as a follow-up (e.g., mp init --vendor-docs).

open_questions.question: For mp init --refresh: should it also refresh config.json / plan.json if the template defaults changed, or just AGENTS.md?
open_questions.answer: mp init --refresh rewrites master-plan/AGENTS.md only — scope is intentionally narrow and predictable. Config drift (config.json / plan.json schema changes) gets a separate doctor check (e.g., mp doctor config-drift) rather than being folded into a doc-refresh flag; folding config rewrites into --refresh is surprising and harder to revert. If schema-level config migration is needed, that's a separate mp config migrate command — out of scope for M194.

work_packages.name: Fix doc references in templates

findings.description: AC-01 and AC-02 verification commands use 'grep -rn ../docs/' which is BRE (Basic Regular Expression). BRE's '.' matches any character, so 'grep ../docs/' matches false positives like 'n/docs/' (from 'plan/docs/') and 'r/docs/' (from 'master-plan/docs/') — both of which are legitimate single-dot segments in toolkit-absolute paths. The spec's verification command would have falsely reported project-relative refs even after the fix. Resolution: I updated the AC verification commands to use the strict regex 'grep -nE \.\./docs/' which requires a literal '..' before '/docs/'. The on-disk spec text still has the original (false-positive-prone) command. Future specs should default to grep -E for these path checks.
findings.author: M194 runner (mavis session mvs_ca0deff7cf7842fa9a4a18fc1e6ed29b)

findings.description: The AC-01 and AC-02 verification commands require a fresh 'mp install' (or 'make install-global') to populate ~/.agents/master-plan/docs/ before they can pass. The 'mp install' code already mirrors the docs/ tree (crates/mp/src/install.rs:1235) so this is automatic on install, but tests run without an explicit install step will see MISS for all doc refs. The 'cargo nextest run -p mp' tests don't depend on this — they only check template content — but the grep + path check the spec calls for does. Resolution: the verification commands are documented as one-liners that the operator runs after install; the test suite (which doesn't depend on the install) is the CI gate. No code change needed.
findings.author: M194 runner (mavis session mvs_ca0deff7cf7842fa9a4a18fc1e6ed29b)

findings.description:
When mp init --refresh is invoked in a non-TTY context without --yes, the command prints a warning to stderr and emits a JSON payload with refresh: "cancelled" + ok: true, then exits 0. The test refresh_in_non_interactive_context_requires_yes explicitly pins this ("non-tty without --yes must cancel, not error"). 

The problem: a script that does  will get a false positive — the exit code is 0 but the file was not rewritten. The user has to read the JSON payload to know the refresh was cancelled.

A non-zero exit code on cancellation (or exit 0 with an explicit ok: false in JSON) would be more honest. Recommend: when --format json and the refresh is cancelled, set ok: false and exit non-zero; when the human output path is used, keep the current behavior (no error, just a warning, since the user can see the message).

Also: the warning printed to stderr is the only signal a CI user gets. The JSON consumers can't see stderr reliably (it goes to a separate stream). The cancelled status should be visible in stdout.
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)
findings.summary: Cancelled refresh returns exit 0, misleading for scripts

findings.description:
The diff_line_counts helper in crates/mp/src/commands/init.rs is set-based (uses HashSet), so it undercounts duplicate added/removed lines. The test diff_line_counts_counts_unique_lines pins this current behavior, but the function is called from prompt_confirm_refresh to give the user a sense of 'how much will change'. A user looking at '(+2 / -1 lines)' for a real 100-line change would be misled into thinking only 3 lines will change.

The function name does not communicate that the count is set-based. Two reasonable fixes: (1) rename to diff_unique_line_counts so the limitation is visible at the call site; (2) switch to a real line-based diff using a similar crate (e.g. the similar crate is already used elsewhere in the project, per a quick grep).

Tradeoff: option 1 is a one-line rename, low risk; option 2 is more invasive but gives the user a faithful diff stat. Recommend option 1 as the minimum, with option 2 as a follow-up if anyone actually relies on the line counts.
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)
findings.summary: diff_line_counts is set-based and undercounts duplicates

findings.description:
AGENTS-TEMPLATE.md line 4 has [../AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) — a project-relative link to the project's own AGENTS.md file (from the master-plan/ subdirectory). This is a deliberate exception: the link points to a sibling file in the project root, not to a toolkit doc. After M194 the rest of the template uses toolkit-absolute paths, so this one relative path stands out.

A reader scanning the template might think this was an oversight. A short HTML comment above the line ('sibling-project link, not a toolkit doc') would clarify. Low-priority polish — the link is correct as-is, but the visual contrast with the surrounding absolute paths invites confusion.
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)
findings.summary: Project-relative AGENTS.md link not documented as an exception

findings.description:
The prompt_confirm_refresh function in crates/mp/src/commands/init.rs reads from stdin and accepts 'y' (yes) or anything-else (no). The test refresh_in_non_interactive_context_requires_yes covers the non-TTY cancel path (which short-circuits the prompt), but the interactive 'user types n' path is untested. A regression that breaks the 'n' handling (e.g. the line is read but the equality check is wrong) would not be caught.

Test would need to pipe a fake stdin (e.g. 'n\n' to /dev/stdin of a child process). Most test frameworks in this repo already use std::process::Command with .stdin(Stdio::piped()) — the pattern is established. Recommend: add a test that pipes 'n' to mp init and asserts refresh status is 'cancelled' and AGENTS.md is unchanged.
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)
findings.summary: Interactive 'no' path in prompt_confirm_refresh is untested

findings.description:
The init_refresh.rs tests cover four paths: (1) refresh rewrites AGENTS.md when --yes is passed; (2) refresh requires an existing plan dir; (3) refresh leaves config.json/plan.json untouched; (4) refresh in a non-TTY context without --yes cancels.

The matrix is missing one path: a non-TTY context WITH --yes. Specifically: a CI script runs  on a project that already has a stale AGENTS.md. The current tests cover this in TTY mode (test 1) but not in non-TTY mode. A regression in the --yes path that only fires when stdin is not a TTY would not be caught.

Test would pipe /dev/null to stdin and run --refresh --yes. Recommend: add a fifth test that runs mp init --refresh --yes with piped stdin and asserts the file is rewritten and refresh status is 'rewritten'.
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)
findings.summary: No test for --refresh in a fresh non-TTY project that has a stale AGENTS.md
